source.title: Prompt Attacks Reveal Superficial Knowledge Removal in Unlearning Methods
source.authors: Yeonwoo Jang; Shariqah Hossain; Ashwin Sreevatsa; Diogo Cruz

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some results are supplied only in figures, but the paper is not cut off or garbled in a way that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether prompt changes retrieve WMDP-bio knowledge after unlearning, using a different prompt-attack evaluation and logit/probe measures.
record.gate_note: The paper tests prompt rephrasings, filler text, translations and 5-shot in-context prompting, and probes residual-stream representations. It does not test fine-tuning on a relearning set, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. Values used only to construct rephrasings are not results. Cited recovery findings from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: It applies black-box prompt attacks (filler text, rephrasings, translations, n-shot) to eight existing WMDP-bio unlearning methods. It measures logit and output accuracy plus residual-stream probes, so its own results bear on whether prompting recovers unlearned knowledge (E), whether unlearning holds against simple attacks (A), and whether knowledge is blocked rather than deleted (C, analysis branch). It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find RMU and TAR robust to prompt attacks, while ELM is vulnerable, especially to Hindi filler (up to 57.3%). They also find output and logit accuracy strongly correlated, so models are not hiding knowledge via formatting, and that many prior retrieval successes are better explained by formatting issues. They describe a trade-off: capability-preserving methods are vulnerable, while robust methods (TAR, GradDiff, RepNoise, RMU+LAT) may owe robustness partly to capability loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates several existing unlearning methods on WMDP-bio and adds prompt-rephrasing, logit and probe analyses; it does not reproduce one original method as the sole intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies by unlearning method and prompt modification: Hindi filler is especially effective for ELM, while RMU, TAR and several other methods show no comparable improvement. Some robust methods have lower tinyMMLU performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Logit-based accuracy is highly correlated with output-token accuracy. The authors argue many prior retrieval successes reflect output-format failures (e.g., RMU answers only about 40% in valid format) rather than hidden knowledge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent unlearning or recovery on multiple-choice benchmarks can be an artifact of answer-format suppression; logit vs output scoring should be compared.

record.peer_reviewed: Socially Responsible Language Modelling Research (SoLaR) Workshop at Conference on Language Modeling (COLM 2025)
record.problems: Most appendix-table results have no uncertainty estimates. Several probe and 5-shot values are only shown in figures, without numerical reporting. The paper does not report paired base-model tinyMMLU values for every checkpoint, limiting direct assessment of capability retention.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap required omitting many separately reported prompt conditions from Appendix B, Tables 1-17, including the remaining translations, variable substitutions, technical-term removal, and filler/rephrasing results. The retained rows prioritize original-prompt and Hindi-filler comparisons across checkpoints, capability scores, probe evidence, 5-shot results, and selected ELM prompt conditions that illustrate prompt sensitivity.

untested.parts: Robustness to fine-tuning, activation edits and quantization attacks; only prompt attacks are tested.
All of it: no relearning fine-tuning.
Activation-direction ablation. Only the probe-based access-vs-deletion analysis is tested.
Jailbreak-style prompts. Rephrasing, filler, translation and n-shot are tested.
All of it: no new counter-method is proposed.

missing.what: Base Zephyr-7B WMDP-bio accuracy of 66.5%, needed as the baseline for A and E rows.
Format split for Zephyr RMU: about 40% of answers in the right format, with about 40% accuracy on those; ELM has about 90% right format at about 30% accuracy.
Output-based (non-logit) accuracies, including ELM Zephyr Hindi-filler output accuracy of 0.5727 versus original 0.3018 logit.

record.verdict_notes: Only prompt attacks are tested; B, D and F are untested. Rows linked to both A and E carry states that describe recovery, so for A an observed recovery counts against the version. Original-prompt rows were relinked to A only. TAR Hindi-filler gains (+2.5 and +3.9 pp) were left absent because the authors call TAR robust. Paired base-model WMDP and tinyMMLU values are missing for most checkpoints, so capability states rest on the authors' statements.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests prompt-attack recovery and reports tinyMMLU capability scores, but does not give a paired base-model tinyMMLU value for every checkpoint.
No fine-tuning or weight training on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples is tested. The 5-shot experiment is in-context prompting, not fine-tuning.
No activation-direction ablation is performed; the study uses linear probes and discusses whether information remains represented.
No low-bit quantization experiment is reported.
The study tests prompt rephrasing, filler text, translation and few-shot in-context prompting; it does not test jailbreaks as a separate attack category.
No new counter-method is proposed and tested against the listed attacks.

labels.label: challenges
labels.reason: The text says probes retrieve no meaningful information after RMU. Figure only.

relation.reason: Its own results bear on versions A, C and E.

tranche.reason: It runs its own prompt attacks, logit analysis and probes on existing unlearning methods. These differ from the original's GCG and probe tests but ask the same question: is the knowledge recoverable?

source_check.notes: Row values match Tables 3-17 (logit). Tables 1-2 give slightly different values for the same Zephyr checkpoints (ELM Hindi filler 0.5711 logit, 57.3% output). The study also translated the questions (11 languages on Zephyr_RMU; Farsi, German and Korean elsewhere) with little or no gain (Zephyr_RMU Hindi 0.2899, Telugu 0.2702 vs 0.3071). No pack row covers these.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: ELM checkpoints tested with Hindi filler text
reader_labels.reason: Hindi filler substantially increases WMDP-bio accuracy after ELM, contrary to the claim that simple attacks do not retrieve knowledge; see r08, r10, r12, r14 and r24.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: RMU, PB&J, RR, TAR, Gradient Difference and RepNoise under Hindi filler
reader_labels.reason: These tested checkpoints show no reported meaningful Hindi-filler recovery; see r02, r04, r06, r16, r18, r20, r22, r26, r28 and r30.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: TAR, Gradient Difference, RepNoise and RMU+LAT capability scores
reader_labels.reason: The authors report reduced tinyMMLU performance for these more robust methods, qualifying the capability-retention part; see r33, r40, r41, r43 and r45.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ELM Zephyr with Hindi filler and residual-stream probes
reader_labels.reason: The authors report high probe accuracy when Hindi filler is used to retrieve the obscured knowledge; see r47.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Hindi filler raises WMDP-bio accuracy markedly over original-prompt scores in the tested ELM checkpoints; see r08, r10, r12, r14 and r24.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ELM checkpoints with English filler or other rephrasings
reader_labels.reason: Some other rephrasings produce modest gains, while poem rephrasing does not; retrieval depends on the prompt modification and checkpoint. See r52-r60.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: non-ELM checkpoints with Hindi filler, and tested 5-shot prompting
reader_labels.reason: Hindi filler does not produce meaningful recovery for the listed non-ELM checkpoints, and the authors say 5-shot prompting was not effective; see r02, r04, r06, r16, r18, r20, r22, r26, r28, r30 and r49-r51.
